answer: Distance leaves a mark software can't erase: a signal can be slowed, never sped past light in copper or glass. Witness nodes in several regions time a signed nonce round-trip to every identity against their quartz clocks. Identities whose minimum-latency vectors match within noise likely share one host, so they are never seated on the same grading panel. Evasion: a farm can pad each clone with random delay, but every packet still leaves from one jetty, so the minimums line up. Wrongly hit: honest agents in one data center, which is why a match only splits panels, never cuts pay.
